meta.title: Cyber eggs
meta.description: Daily free-token collector. The egg button in the left sidebar opens a panel with four tabs. Market lists sources in three tiers: the top row 'Most used 🔥' holds the three most popular ones (SiliconFlow, Zhipu GLM, OpenRouter), followed by three 'Editor picks 荐' (Groq, Gemini AI Studio, ModelScope), then the rest. Every card states the rough daily allowance ('about 50 requests/day', '2000 calls per model/day', '1M tokens per model'), whether you can register from mainland China (directly / needs a proxy / needs a foreign card), and a longer note on which models are free, rate limits, and setup gotchas. Install asks for that site's API key, asks the endpoint for its own model list, and registers the result as a model provider named '<site> · Cyber eggs' for the composer's model picker. A live 'Global free-model radar' reads OpenRouter's public model API, lists every model priced zero for input and output, and marks models that appeared since the last check; the Refresh eggs button re-pulls it at any time. The catalogue is not limited to the built-in entries: My relays registers any New API / One API style relay site with a connection test and a claim action, and Custom feeds accepts any JSON URL ({"sources":[{"id","name","baseURL","api","daily","access","signupUrl"}]}) whose entries merge in on refresh and get a new mark, so new eggs arrive without a plugin update. A 'No-key' tab adds the free models of Kilo's public gateway: Enable or Enable all puts them in the model picker with no sign-up and no key. DSH's adapter always sends an auth header while that gateway requires none, so the plugin forwards through 127.0.0.1 and strips it — dsh-our-free-model is not involved and conversations are not stored; the free pool may log prompts upstream, so never send sensitive content. Auto claim stores one daily time (default 09:00) and checks in to every enabled relay while DSH runs, with an optional same-day catch-up; History keeps each result. Keys and tokens go to the local credential store, never to cordis.patch.yml; relay, radar and feed state lives in <DSH_HOME>/cyber-egg/state.json. Limitations: sites requiring human verification, a CAPTCHA, or a WeChat mini-program login cannot be checked in automatically; quotas and registration policies change at any time, so the figures are approximate and the provider's own page wins; daily claims need DSH to be running. It also installs inside DSH Go (Android): copy the package to the phone, run `dsh plugin --profile web add file:/sdcard/Download/cyber-egg-latest.tgz` in the app terminal, then restart the engine.
